purpose: The catalogue of paper an institution produces. A document form says why a record exists, who writes it for whom, and what it is naturally good at revealing or hiding. The S2 author cuts the story into these forms; the S3 author writes inside one form at a time. Abstract only: no story.

forms.name: incident report
forms.purpose: the institution's official account of an event
forms.author_kind: staff on duty or a department
forms.reveals: the official sequence and what the author was required to record
forms.hides: what the author chose not to record; anything outside the form's fields
forms.voice_tip: fields filled in order; times to the minute; passive where blame might fall

forms.name: duty roster or rota
forms.purpose: who is meant to be where and when
forms.reveals: presence, absence, swaps, patterns
forms.voice_tip: a grid; initials or codes; amendments in a different hand

forms.name: requisition or order slip
forms.purpose: asking for a thing
forms.reveals: intention through objects, quantities and urgency
forms.voice_tip: quantities, unit codes, a justification line kept short

forms.name: maintenance or service log
forms.purpose: recording work done on equipment or a building
forms.reveals: physical state, constraints, timing of faults
forms.voice_tip: terse, technical, abbreviations the trade uses

forms.name: meeting minutes
forms.purpose: a record of what was decided
forms.reveals: power, who spoke, what was deferred
forms.hides: what was said off the record; arguments compressed to one line
forms.voice_tip: names by role or initials; action points; the euphemism of agreement

forms.name: personal letter or note
forms.purpose: one person writing to another for their own reasons
forms.reveals: feeling, history, the relationship
forms.hides: what both already know and so never say
forms.voice_tip: the writer's own habits; references the reader would understand and the player must infer

forms.name: internal memo
forms.purpose: instructing or informing within the institution
forms.reveals: policy, priorities, tension between departments
forms.voice_tip: subject line, distribution list, a tone calibrated to rank

forms.name: invoice, receipt or account line
forms.purpose: money changing hands
forms.reveals: time, quantity, payer, place
forms.voice_tip: numbers, dates, reference codes; no commentary

forms.name: interview or call transcript
forms.purpose: a verbatim record of speech
forms.author_kind: a transcriber; speakers are named people
forms.reader_kind: a file or a reviewing department
forms.reveals: voice, evasion, what a person volunteers
forms.hides: tone and gesture unless the transcriber notes them
forms.voice_tip: each speaker sounds like their sheet; hesitations marked sparingly; transcriber notes in brackets

forms.name: sign-in, visitor or access log
forms.purpose: who entered and left
forms.author_kind: a desk, a system, or the visitors themselves
forms.reveals: presence and times, handwriting, who signed for whom
forms.voice_tip: columns; repeated entries; one entry that breaks the pattern

forms.name: inventory or stock count
forms.purpose: what is held
forms.reveals: what moved, what is missing
forms.voice_tip: counts, discrepancies explained in a word

forms.name: handover note
forms.purpose: telling the next shift what they need to know
forms.reveals: what the author thought mattered at the end of a shift
forms.hides: what they were too tired or too careful to write
forms.voice_tip: informal, abbreviated, first names, small worries

forms.name: complaint or grievance form
forms.purpose: formally objecting to something
forms.reveals: a grievance with dates and names
forms.voice_tip: a person trying to sound formal; the form's boxes are too small

forms.name: department analysis report
forms.purpose: a department's processing of an item
forms.reveals: raw findings and the department's assessment as separate sections
forms.hides: the analyst's bias, unless the reader looks for it
forms.voice_tip: findings plain and measured; assessment in the department's voice profile

forms.name: telephone message slip
forms.purpose: relaying a call
forms.reveals: a time, a caller, a short message
forms.voice_tip: printed fields, a hurried hand, the caller's words compressed

forms.name: diary, calendar or appointment page
forms.purpose: a person planning their time
forms.reveals: intentions, appointments, private shorthand
forms.voice_tip: private abbreviations; crossings out; nothing explained

forms.name: photograph with caption or label
forms.purpose: recording what a place or thing looked like
forms.reveals: physical arrangement at a moment
forms.voice_tip: caption in the institution's filing style; legible text only as real overlay text

forms.name: notice or bulletin
forms.purpose: telling everyone something
forms.reveals: the institution's public face and its routines
forms.voice_tip: cheerful or firm, generic on purpose

forms.name: application or form with fields
forms.purpose: requesting permission or a benefit
forms.reveals: facts the person must state about themselves
forms.hides: facts the form does not ask for
forms.voice_tip: boxes, tick marks, a short free-text line that says more than intended

forms.name: delivery or dispatch note
forms.purpose: a thing moving from one place to another
forms.reveals: route, time, signature, condition
forms.hides: what happened between pickup and drop
forms.voice_tip: reference numbers, signature lines, a condition note

techniques.name: Re-contextualised mundane
techniques.use: A routine record becomes decisive only once something else is known.
techniques.risk: The player skips it. Give it a second route.

techniques.name: Contradictory attachment
techniques.use: A summary says one thing; the attached raw data says another.
techniques.risk: The player reads only the summary. Keep both on one record.

techniques.name: Missing entry
techniques.use: A sequence with one gap; the gap is the evidence.
techniques.risk: Reads as a bug. Establish the normal sequence in two places first.

techniques.name: Escalating requisition
techniques.use: A series of requests that tells an arc through objects.

techniques.name: Over-expressed account
techniques.use: A person gives far more detail than the form needs.
techniques.risk: Trope if overt. The extra detail must be ordinary and checkable.

techniques.name: Cross-reference cipher
techniques.use: Two records are meaningless alone and clear together.
techniques.risk: Connection too obscure. Share a reference, a code or a time.

techniques.name: The lure
techniques.use: Concrete detail that grounds the world and sits beside the real clue.
techniques.risk: Frustration if lures outnumber clues badly.

techniques.name: Sudden brevity
techniques.use: A habitually long writer writes one line.
techniques.risk: Needs the long voice established first.

techniques.name: Epistolary silence
techniques.use: Letters that go unanswered, or a reply that ignores the question.
techniques.risk: Player assumes a missing record. Make the silence itself visible.

techniques.name: Innocent observer
techniques.use: Someone records what they saw without understanding it.
techniques.risk: Forced naivety. The observer's attention must fit their sheet.

techniques.name: Overlapping jurisdictions
techniques.use: Departments disagree on paper about who owns a problem.
techniques.risk: Office drama crowding the case. Tie it to a fact.

techniques.name: Chronological disconnect
techniques.use: Records whose dates only make sense once reordered.
techniques.risk: Too subtle. Dates must be exact and consistent.

techniques.name: Eloquence of omission
techniques.use: What an official record leaves out is the tell.
techniques.risk: Unprovable. The omission must be checkable against another record.
